newsitem.title: UK: Hambros ups profits, sees banking progress.
newsitem.headline: Hambros ups profits, sees banking progress.

text.p: British investment banking group Hambros Plc on Wednesday announced improved annual pre-tax profits but said the return on capital of its banking division remained inadequate, although progress was being made.

Hambros made profits before tax of 64.7 million pounds ($105.9 million) for the year to March 31, up from 20.6 million pounds the previous year. Earnings per share were 12.5 pence against a 7.6 pence loss and the total dividend was unchanged at 7.5 pence.

Hambros said it was still awaiting an independent report on its role in the failed takeover attempt of mutually-owned supermarkets-to-funeral parlours group the Co-operative Wholesale Society (CWS) by entrepreneur Andrew Regan.

In April Hambros was forced to make an unreserved apology to CWS for its involvement in the discredited takevoer bid. Hambros' banking group announced reduced exceptional costs of 9.0 million pounds, from 12.2 million, which included a provision for the costs of the CWS affair.

"Although the return on capital earned by the banking group in the past year was still inadequate, we have made progress towards our medium term objectives in each main area of activity," chief executive Sir Chips Keswick said in a statement.

Keswick said prospsects for Hambro Countrywide, the separately quoted estate agents business in which it has a majority shareholding, were excellent, the investment group had made an important contribution to the results and there had been underlying growth from Hambro Insurance Services. ($ = 0.610 British Pounds)
